title: Etale sum extension and arbitrary tensor pullback
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $j:Z\to X$ be a representable etale morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$, and let $h:X_1\to X$ be any morphism. Put $Z_1=Z\times_XX_1$, with $j_1:Z_1\to X_1$ and $h_Z:Z_1\to Z$. Use small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], their module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], canonical module tensor pullback and direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $j_!$ for the exact left adjoint to exact slice restriction $j^*$: it is module sheafification of the presheaf $W\mapsto\bigoplus_{a:W\to Z\text{ over }X}M(W,a)$; its counit $j_!j^*N\to N$ evaluates each summand by restriction. Use the analogous definitions for $j_1$ and for etale composites.
There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$h^*j_!M\simeq j_{1!}h_Z^*M.$$
It agrees with the geometric-fibre direct-sum identification after tensoring the structure rings, preserves the evaluation counits after the canonical comparison $h_Z^*j^*\simeq j_1^*h^*$, and is compatible with composition of etale restrictions and their extension-by-zero counits. Both $j^*$ and $j_!$ preserve K-flat complexes with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]; they act termwise on complexes. Consequently the specified ordinary comparison induces
$$Lh^*j_!\simeq j_{1!}Lh_Z^*$$
on unbounded derived categories, computed by that same summand formula on flat-term K-flat resolutions. These comparisons preserve finite sums, the counits for nested etale slices, and the canonical shift maps. No flatness of $h$, boundedness of the complexes, quasi-compactness, or finiteness of geometric fibres is assumed.

Arbitrary structural-ring tensor and sum-extension compatibility is the agent-written consequence of these formulas.

proof.text: Use the enlarged etale ringed-site model, so $Z$ is an object of $\mathcal C_X$ and $\mathcal C_Z=\mathcal C_X/Z$ with the restricted structure ring; do the same for $Z_1\to X_1$. The localized module adjunction gives the exact functors $j_!\dashv j^*$ and $j_{1!}\dashv j_1^*$ with the specified sheafified sum formula. Its counit sends a section in the lift-$a$ summand to that section of $N(W)$: this is the map corresponding to $\mathrm{id}_{j^*N}$ in the adjunction. Its unit inserts a section into the identity-lift summand on the localized site, since this map followed by evaluation is the identity on each summand. The chart tensor realization identifies these restrictions with the canonical module pullbacks in the statement.

Let $u:\mathrm{id}\to j^*j_!$ be the preceding unit and $v_1:j_{1!}j_1^*\to\mathrm{id}$ the primed counit. Ringed pullback composition for $jh_Z=hj_1$ gives $\chi:h_Z^*j^*\simeq j_1^*h^*$; on local tensors it is the associative map multiplying the structural scalars. Define
$$\beta_M:j_{1!}h_Z^*M\xrightarrow{j_{1!}h_Z^*u_M}j_{1!}h_Z^*j^*j_!M\xrightarrow{j_{1!}\chi_{j_!M}}j_{1!}j_1^*h^*j_!M\xrightarrow{v_{1,h^*j_!M}}h^*j_!M.$$
Every arrow is a specified natural module map; thus this defines a natural transformation before any stalk test. The composition and structural-ring identifications here are those fixed by the enlarged ringed model and the chart-unit tensor formula, so no arbitrary pullback isomorphism has been substituted.

Fix $\bar x_1:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X_1$ and put $\bar x=h\bar x_1$, $R=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{X_1,\bar x_1}$. By the fibre-product universal property, lifts $\bar z_1$ of $\bar x_1$ to $Z_1$ correspond bijectively to lifts $\bar z$ of $\bar x$ to $Z$, all with the same field $\Omega$. The sum-stalk formula and the pullback-stalk formula identify the stalks of the source and target of $\beta_M$ with
$$\bigoplus_{\bar z}(M_{\bar z}\otimes_R B),\qquad (\bigoplus_{\bar z}M_{\bar z})\otimes_R B.$$
The etale stalk-ring isomorphisms identify the scalar map for $h_Z$ with $R\to B$. The identity-summand unit and evaluation counit from step 1 show that $\beta$ sends $m\otimes b$ in the $\bar z$-summand to $\iota_{\bar z}(m)\otimes b$. Its inverse sends $(\sum\iota_{\bar z}m_{\bar z})\otimes b$ to $\sum\iota_{\bar z}(m_{\bar z}\otimes b)$; the sums have finite support, and balancing over $R$ proves this is well defined. The formulas are inverse on generators. Conservative geometric stalks now show $\beta$ is an isomorphism; define the required comparison to be $\beta^{-1}$.

For a module $N$ on $X$, put $M=j^*N$. At a geometric stalk the counit $j_!j^*N\to N$ is the fold map: the germ in every lift summand is evaluated to that same germ of $N$. Both composites in the base-change counit square therefore send $m\otimes b$ in each lift summand to $m\otimes b$. This proves the required square, using stalk detection of equality. For $T\xrightarrow{k}Z\xrightarrow{j}X$ etale, the canonical adjunction-composition isomorphism $j_!k_!\simeq(jk)_!$ flattens the two sum labels: a lift to $Z$ followed by a lift to $T$ is a lift to $T$. Evaluation in two stages and evaluation after flattening both send a germ to itself. Base change relabels the same pair of lifts, so its comparison commutes with flattening and these nested counits. On a tensor with iterated scalars, both paths give $m\otimes bc$ under the associative structural-ring maps. Thus these are the canonical composition comparisons, not just objectwise isomorphisms.

proof.text:
On the enlarged localized site use the natural projection isomorphism
$$ (j_!F)\otimes H\simeq j_!(F\otimes j^*H).$$
If $F$ is flat, applying this to a short exact sequence in $H$ proves $j_!F$ flat: $j^*$ is exact, tensoring with $F$ is exact, and $j_!$ is exact. The functor $j_!$ preserves small sums since it is a left adjoint. Hence for complexes its projection isomorphisms sum, in total degree $n$, over all $p+q=n$ to
$$(j_!P)\otimes H\simeq j_!(P\otimes j^*H).$$
Naturality in $P^p$ and $H^q$ makes this an isomorphism of complexes: it commutes separately with $d_P\otimes1$ and $1\otimes d_H$, and additivity preserves the factor $(-1)^p$. If $H$ is acyclic, exact restriction makes $j^*H$ acyclic; K-flatness of $P$ makes $P\otimes j^*H$ acyclic; exactness of $j_!$ makes its extension acyclic. Thus $j_!$ preserves K-flat complexes, and the flatness argument gives preservation of flat terms. This argument uses direct sums in every degree, never products or boundedness.

proof.text: Restriction to the localized ringed site preserves K-flatness by the ringed-site restriction theorem. For a K-flat complex with flat terms it also preserves flat terms, by the ringed-topos pullback theorem applied to the localization morphism, whose structural ring map is the identity on the restricted ring. These assertions apply to $j,j_1$ and their etale composites. For $h,h_Z$, the same pullback theorem gives preservation of flat-term K-flat complexes despite their possibly nonflat structural-ring maps.

For any complex $K$ on $Z$, choose a flat-term K-flat quasi-isomorphism $P\to K$. Step 5 makes $j_!P\to j_!K$ such a resolution. The ringed-topos derived-pullback theorem and exact-functor factorization therefore compute $Lh^*j_!K$ by $h^*j_!P$ and $j_{1!}Lh_Z^*K$ by $j_{1!}h_Z^*P$. Apply step 3 degreewise to $P$; naturality makes it a chain isomorphism. To descend it naturally, take the two derived composite functors precomposed with $Q:K(\mathcal O_Z)\to D(\mathcal O_Z)$. On flat-term K-flat objects their comparison is the displayed chain isomorphism conjugated by the canonical resolution-computation maps, natural in all maps between such objects. The resolving-class natural-transformation lemma extends it to all of $K(\mathcal O_Z)$: replacements exist by the resolution theorem, and quasi-isomorphisms have a right calculus of fractions. The localization universal property then descends it uniquely to $D(\mathcal O_Z)$. Applying this also to the inverse gives inverse transformations, since on a quasi-isomorphism $P\to K$ naturality conjugates the composite at $K$ to the identity composite at $P$. This produces the stated derived natural isomorphism computed by the specified ordinary comparison.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); derived.tex Tag 05RT and categories.tex Tag 04VK for the localization step

proof.text: Each ordinary comparison is additive and is defined degreewise, so it commutes with finite sums. It commutes with the shift by $n$: both complexes in degree $r$ use the comparison on $P^{r+n}$ and both differentials acquire the same factor $(-1)^n$. The same assertion holds for the evaluation counits, which are degreewise maps. Flat-term K-flat complexes remain such after finite sums, shifts and the etale functors from steps 5--6; for shifts the K-flat test is the shifted acyclic tensor test, and for finite sums it is the direct sum of finitely many acyclic tests. For the derived evaluation square resolve $N$ on $X$ by such a $P$; its restriction and the successive etale extensions are adapted models by steps 5--6. Step 4 is therefore literally the required counit and composition equality on these models. Step 7's descent and its inverse are fixed on all these models, so naturality with a resolution quasi-isomorphism proves the equalities for all derived objects, including the specified shift and finite-sum comparisons. Empty fibres give the zero sum, and arbitrarily many lifts cause no difficulty because every sum element has finite support.
